correctness.rationale: Explicit GP(10,2) graph with 30 edges; exhaustive perfect-matching recursion gives 36 ten-edge facets and 30,504 faces. Sequential toggle matching over all nonempty faces contains 15,238 pairs and exactly 1 critical 0-cell, 3 critical 2-cells and 23 critical 3-cells. The complete oriented Hasse graph of 163,650 incidences is acyclic. Signed gradient-path recursion yields the 3-by-23 integer boundary with gcds of minors (1,1,2), therefore Smith factors (1,1,2). The simply connected three-dimensional Morse CW model splits as M(Z/2,2) wedge twenty 3-spheres. Independent elementary face collapses and modular calculations over F2,F3,F5,F101 agree; all code and expected outputs are embedded. Computational proof is finite and exhaustive, not inference from sample data.

value.rationale: The dodecahedral graph is the smallest fullerene and a canonical cubic symmetric example; its perfect-matching complex has a natural chemical/combinatorial definition via 36 Kekulé structures. A nontrivial degree-two Moore summand gives integral torsion and a complete homotopy classification, sharply distinguishing it from the larger ordinary matching complex. Exact, motivated finite classification is structurally informative and reproducible; no downstream general theorem is claimed.
